title: Offline shadow comparison execution: T1/T2/T4 scenarios with persisted diff reports
objective: Execute the comparison harness across a representative set of T1, T2, and T4 AppraisalInput scenarios using a deterministic LLM stub (no live API calls), collect one ComparisonReport per scenario, serialize all reports to a structured JSON file on disk, and produce a summary table that counts pass/degraded/fail verdicts by tick type.
exact_scope: A new test module at back/tests/test_p30_t5_shadow_comparison_run.py executes the harness against at least 9 representative scenarios (3 per active tick type: T1, T2, T4-with-event). The shadow runner's _call_llm is replaced by a deterministic in-process stub for every test — no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required and no network call is made. Each scenario captures one ComparisonReport. All reports are serialized to back/tests/fixtures/p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json using model_dump. A summary dict — keyed by tick type, counting SEMANTIC_PASS / SEMANTIC_DEGRADED / STRUCTURAL_FAIL verdicts — is also written to the same fixture file alongside the raw reports. The stub is defined inside the test module itself; it is not a new production module. No changes are made to any engine, settlement, domain model, or existing test file.
constraints: No live LLM API call is made at any point — _call_llm must be patched with a deterministic stub via unittest.mock.patch for every scenario
No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable is required to run the tests
AppraisalSignal v1 definition must not be touched
Settlement engines must not be touched
The stub must live inside the test module, not in a new production module under back/app/
The fixture file (p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json) must be written only by the test module; no new production-side file I/O code is added
All existing tests must continue to pass after this task is implemented
The comparison harness, shadow runner, and acceptance rules modules must not be modified
T3, T5, T6, T7, T8 deferred ticks are not in scope for scenario execution
acceptance_criteria: Running pytest back/tests/test_p30_t5_shadow_comparison_run.py passes with zero failures and no network calls
The fixture file back/tests/fixtures/p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json is created (or overwritten) when the test module runs
The fixture file contains a top-level key 'reports' holding a list of at least 9 serialized ComparisonReport dicts
Each report dict contains the fields: world_day, agent_id, tick_type, shadow_llm_used, shadow_failure_reason, and a verdict with overall, structural_failures, semantic_deviations, and field_results
The fixture file contains a top-level key 'summary' holding per-tick-type verdict counts with keys SEMANTIC_PASS, SEMANTIC_DEGRADED, and STRUCTURAL_FAIL
At least one scenario per tick type (T1, T2, T4-with-event) produces shadow_llm_used=True (the stub returns a valid JSON response)
At least one scenario per tick type produces shadow_llm_used=False (the stub raises an exception or returns invalid JSON), capturing fallback behavior

At least one scenario where the stub returns a response that differs from the deterministic baseline (e.g. a different valence), so the report captures a semantic deviation with overall=SEMANTIC_DEGRADED
At least one T4 scenario uses an input with social_event_context present (so the deterministic baseline has absorption=surface, not none)
At least one T4 scenario uses an input without social_event_context (so the deterministic baseline has absorption=none)
required_tests: Importing the test module causes no network calls and no side effects
Running the full scenario suite writes the fixture file to back/tests/fixtures/p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json
The fixture file has a 'reports' list with at least 9 entries
The fixture file has a 'summary' dict covering at least the three tick types: information_exposure, social_interaction, relationship_shift
For each T1 scenario with a valid stub response, the report shows shadow_llm_used=True and tick_type=information_exposure
For each T2 scenario with a valid stub response, the report shows shadow_llm_used=True, tick_type=social_interaction, and the relational_context is echoed in the report's tick_type field
For a T4-with-event scenario where the stub returns a response that exactly matches the deterministic baseline, the verdict.overall is SEMANTIC_PASS
For a T4-with-event scenario where the stub returns a response with a different valence than the deterministic baseline, the verdict.overall is SEMANTIC_DEGRADED
For a T4-without-event scenario where the stub returns a valid surface-absorption response, the verdict.overall is STRUCTURAL_FAIL (LLM says surface but baseline says none)
For any scenario where the stub raises a connection error, the report shows shadow_llm_used=False and shadow_failure_reason is a non-empty string
For any scenario where the stub returns unparseable text, the report shows shadow_llm_used=False and the deterministic fallback output is used
The summary dict counts are consistent with the individual report verdicts (sum of per-tick counts equals number of reports for that tick type)
non_goals: Do not implement a live LLM call path or require the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Do not add any LLM stub or mock to a production module under back/app/
Do not run T3, T5, T6, T7, or T8 scenarios
Do not modify the comparison harness, shadow runner, acceptance rules, prompt schema, or response parser
Do not modify any settlement engine or domain model
Do not produce a UI view, dashboard component, or API endpoint for the results
Do not analyze or interpret the diff results beyond counting verdict categories in the summary
Do not modify vision.md or road_map.md
